homeTitle: Uraboros: public-source research and Telegram monitoring
homeDescription: Explore public sources, collect posts and comments, monitor selected Telegram channels and receive exports through the bot. Discover URABOROS capabilities and limitations.
heroText: Find publications and collect posts and comments into usable exports. Follow a topic in selected Telegram sources, then return to the website or bot for the results.
freeNote: A free plan with limits is available. Your account shows the available usage and subscription conditions.
accountNote: This page describes the tool. Using it requires an account with verified email and is subject to your plan limits.
catalogTitle: Choose a tool for your task
catalogDescription: Learn what input to provide, what results to expect and which limitations matter. No registration needed to explore.
footer: Search, collection and analysis of public data. Tools are actively developed in beta.
previewNote: Workflow illustration, not live results. Opening this page does not start data collection.

sources.title: You choose the sources
sources.text: Accessible groups or channels and the topic you want to follow.

collection.title: The service checks new messages
collection.text: Periodically collects matches by keyword or sender ID.

result.title: You work with the findings
result.text: Messages on the website, Excel or JSON reports, alerts through your linked bot.

scenariosLabel: More than a list of tools
scenariosTitle: Start with what you want to learn

monitor.title: Follow a topic
monitor.text: Monitor selected Telegram sources and return to matching messages instead of checking each chat manually.

research.title: Collect material for analysis
research.text: Export YouTube comments or posts from supported social platforms to study a discussion and develop your own conclusions.

check.title: Check a website and its context
check.text: Review HTTP, DNS, SSL and SEO signals. Get a starting point for technical investigation, not an unsupported security verdict.

expectationsTitle: A research tool, not a promise to find everything
expectationsText: URABOROS helps collect and organize accessible data. Coverage depends on the source, its policies and the availability of publications.

access.question: What can I explore without an account?
access.answer: Capabilities, use cases and limitations are public. Search, collection, history and personal notifications require signing in and verifying your email.

coverage.question: Does this search the entire internet in real time?
coverage.answer: No. Modules use supported sources and their APIs. Telegram tracking periodically checks selected accessible groups and channels without joining them. Source restrictions and delays can affect results.

data.question: Can I return to results later?
data.answer: Parser runs have history and repeat downloads until retention expires. Tracking has its own retention rules. Analytics reports can be temporary; each capability page explains its limitations.

ctaTitle: Start with one task of your own
ctaText: Create an account, verify your email and choose a module. History and saved queries help you return to your work.

telegram-tracking.title: Telegram monitoring
telegram-tracking.summary: Periodically find new messages by keyword or sender ID in selected groups and channels. Receive alerts and download a report.
telegram-tracking.example: Collect topic mentions from selected industry channels
telegram-tracking.audience: For analysts, editors and researchers who need a growing collection of messages from specific sources.
telegram-tracking.input: A task name, up to {sources} accessible groups or channels, one per line, and either a keyword or a numeric Telegram sender ID. The service checks source accessibility before creating the task.
telegram-tracking.result: Matching messages with dates, sources and links where available. Excel or JSON reports covering the task lifetime, website notifications and optional alerts through your linked bot.
telegram-tracking.step1: Open Telegram → Tracking and create a task with sources and a search condition.
telegram-tracking.step2: Optionally enable bot alerts. The first check is scheduled after creation, not performed instantly.
telegram-tracking.step3: Review messages, download reports, pause or renew the task.
telegram-tracking.limit:
The base check interval is {hours} hours, increasing with load up to {maxHours} hours; Telegram restrictions or outages may delay it further. The service does not join chats or unlock private sources. Messages deleted before a check may be missed.
A task lasts {months} month(s) and can be renewed. Data is kept throughout its lifetime and for {days} days after completion. Pausing does not extend its lifetime; the paused period is not backfilled after resuming. Task capacity depends on your plan.

telegram.title: Telegram search and collection
telegram.summary: Search messages, explore source activity and collect posts with comments for further work in Excel or JSON.
telegram.example: Build a collection of channel posts for a selected period
telegram.audience: For studying discussions, preparing research material and comparing available activity metrics.
telegram.input: An accessible channel or group, a query and parameters for the selected mode. Analytics and collection forms provide the supported sampling controls.
telegram.result: Search results, analytics summaries or background collection of posts and comments. Parser runs support history, stopping and repeat Excel/JSON downloads.
telegram.step1: Open Telegram and choose search, analytics or collection.
telegram.step2: Provide a source and parameters. For background collection, follow the run status.
telegram.step3: Explore the results or download the export from run history.
telegram.limit: Access depends on the source and Telegram restrictions. The service does not expose private or deleted messages. Parser files are retained for {parserDays} days; analytics reports are temporary and are not stored parser exports.

youtube.title: YouTube search and comments
youtube.summary: Find videos, review available content metrics and collect comments with replies into a structured export.
youtube.example: Study feedback under a product video
youtube.audience: For creators, editors and analysts who want to work with discussions beyond the video page.
youtube.input: A search phrase, video URL or ID, or a channel for the selected mode. Configure collection parameters in the parser form.
youtube.result: Search results, summaries of accessible data and Excel/JSON exports of comments and replies. Completed and stopped runs remain available in history.
youtube.step1: Find a video through search or open the parser with its ID.
youtube.step2: Configure comment collection and start the task.
youtube.step3: Open history and download the result for your own analysis.
youtube.limit: Results depend on YouTube API quotas and video/comment availability. This is not access to private YouTube Studio analytics. Parser files are retained for {parserDays} days.

bluesky.title: Bluesky research
bluesky.summary: Find posts and profiles, explore discussions, reactions and public connections. Collect profile and activity data.
bluesky.example: Explore a topic and the activity of its participants
bluesky.audience: For public-community researchers and Bluesky content analysts.
bluesky.input: A query, profile or topic depending on the mode. Supported profile identifiers include handles and DIDs.
bluesky.result: Posts, discussion threads, accessible likes, reposts and account connections. Analytics and background collection with history and Excel/JSON exports.
bluesky.step1: Choose Bluesky search, analytics or the parser.
bluesky.step2: Enter a profile or query and explore available context.
bluesky.step3: To keep a dataset, run collection and download its file from history.
bluesky.limit: Coverage depends on the API, record visibility and collection limits. A public connection does not prove a real-world relationship. Parser files are retained for {parserDays} days.

mastodon.title: Mastodon research
mastodon.summary: Search accounts, posts and hashtags, explore discussion context and collect accessible posts with comments.
mastodon.example: Collect a selected account's posts for research
mastodon.audience: For working with public federated data through the connected Mastodon server.
mastodon.input: An account, query or hashtag for the selected mode. Resolving remote profiles depends on the connected server.
mastodon.result: Accounts and posts, discussion context, analytics summaries and parser exports in Excel/JSON.
mastodon.step1: Open Mastodon and choose a mode.
mastodon.step2: Enter an account or topic and check the available results.
mastodon.step3: Start collection if you need an export, then return through history.
mastodon.limit: One Mastodon server cannot see the entire federation. Post visibility, server policies and API limits affect results. Parser files are retained for {parserDays} days.

site-intel.title: Website checks and SEO
site-intel.summary: Inspect HTTP, DNS, SSL and domain information. Review technical SEO signals, links and recommendations for accessible pages.
site-intel.example: Perform an initial technical review of a website
site-intel.audience: For website owners, developers and analysts who need a starting point for further checks.
site-intel.input: A public domain or URL. Choose reachability checks, domain information, analytics or an SEO audit.
site-intel.result: Technical metrics, detected signals and recommendations. Analytics and SEO audit results support HTML reports.
site-intel.step1: Provide a public website and choose a check.
site-intel.step2: Wait for results and review individual signals, not just the score.
site-intel.step3: Open or download the available HTML report for further work.
site-intel.limit: Results reflect the time of the check and a bounded crawl. This is not a comprehensive security audit, a guarantee of trustworthiness or a search-ranking prediction. Reports are temporary, not an archive of parser exports.

news-media-intel.title: News and media search
news-media-intel.summary: Bring available news about a topic into one collection, explore publication timelines and recurring themes.
news-media-intel.example: Build an initial view of how an event is covered
news-media-intel.audience: For editors and researchers who need a starting collection of links, not a promise of a complete media archive.
news-media-intel.input: A topic, brand, person or event and the available search parameters.
news-media-intel.result: Mentions with partial deduplication, a timeline, frequent topics and an approximate dictionary-based sentiment summary.
news-media-intel.step1: Enter a topic in News & Media Intel.
news-media-intel.step2: Review publications, sources and their distribution over time.
news-media-intel.step3: Visit the original sources and verify context before drawing conclusions.
news-media-intel.limit: This searches available news APIs/RSS, rather than monitoring a topic automatically on a schedule. Sentiment is heuristic, not proof of an author's position. Parser run history and exports are not implemented for this module.

shifr.title: Shifr utilities
shifr.summary: Compute hashes, transform text, extract indicators from text fragments and inspect JWT structure.
shifr.example: Extract domains and IP addresses from a text fragment
shifr.audience: Supporting operations for technical analysis and learning, alongside the main tools.
shifr.input: Text and an operation: hashing, transformation, IOC extraction, JWT inspection or a classic cipher.
shifr.result: Transformed output, detected indicators or a parsed token structure. No separate background collection job.
shifr.step2: Enter non-secret text and set the parameters.
shifr.step3: Inspect the result and use it in your task.
shifr.limit: Do not enter active passwords, private keys or production tokens. JWT inspection does not establish authenticity, and classic ciphers are not intended to protect sensitive data.

telegram-bot.title: URABOROS Telegram bot
telegram-bot.summary: Receive notifications you opted into and collection files in Telegram. Open the workspace from the bot menu.
telegram-bot.example: Receive a finished export without checking the website manually
telegram-bot.audience: For website users who prefer receiving files and notifications in their messenger.
telegram-bot.input: A website account with verified email. Create a link in Telegram settings, open it in the bot and confirm the connection on the website.
telegram-bot.result: An inline menu, available files from your own runs, tracking reports and notifications according to your preferences. Automatic delivery of new exports is a separate opt-in.
telegram-bot.step1: Open Telegram settings on the website and start linking.
telegram-bot.step2: Start the bot using the provided link, then return to the website and confirm your Telegram ID.
telegram-bot.step3: Choose notifications and automatic delivery or request an available file through the menu.
telegram-bot.limit: The bot does not bypass plan limits or restore deleted exports. WebApp opens the website with its normal authentication, not automatic sign-in. Copies already sent to Telegram are not removed when the website cleans up files. Bot availability depends on the service operator's configuration.
